funnel.pnrHelpTitle: How do I find my booking reference?
funnel.pnrHelpLong: Your booking reference (PNR) is a unique code the airline uses for your reservation. You'll find it on your e-ticket or in any email or document the airline sent you. It usually has 6 characters, letters and/or numbers (e.g. DF87G2). Don't include spaces.

rights.title: Вашите права при закъснения, отмени и свръхрезервации
rights.intro: Регламент ЕС ЕО 261/2004 защитава пътниците, излитащи от летище в ЕС или пристигащи в ЕС с авиокомпания от ЕС.
rights.delayText: От 3 часа закъснение при пристигане може да имате право на фиксирано обезщетение.
rights.cancelText: Освен ако не е уведомено поне 14 дни предварително или поради извънредни обстоятелства, отмяната дава право на обезщетение.
rights.overbookingText: Принудителният отказан достъп се обезщетява независимо от закъснението.

faq.q1: How much compensation can I claim?
faq.a1: Depending on the flight distance, Regulation EC 261/2004 provides fixed compensation of €250, €400 or €600 per passenger.
faq.q2: How much does Air Assist cost?
faq.a2: Nothing upfront. We charge a 30% commission only if we win — you keep 70%. No win, no fee.
faq.a3: Flights departing from an EU airport, or arriving in the EU on an EU airline, that were delayed 3+ hours, cancelled or overbooked.
faq.q4: How long does a claim take?
faq.a4: It depends on the airline: many cases settle within a few weeks, some negotiations take a few months. We keep you informed throughout.
faq.q5: How far back can I claim?
faq.a5: In most EU countries you can claim for flights from the past 2 to 3 years, depending on national law.
